title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X = U_{0,3,Q̄} = P^1_{Q̄} minus {0,1,∞}. Γ = N_{0,3} = Γ_Q × S_3, where Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) and S_3 is the group of symmetries of {0,1,∞}. M̂ = Π̂_{0,3}^{ab} is the profinite abelianization of the geometric fundamental group. It is free of rank 2 and isomorphic to Ẑ(1) ⊗ (Z^3/diagonal), with S_3 permuting the three cusp loops. M̃ = M_{0,3}/[Π̂_{0,3}, Π̂_{0,3}] is the 'metabelian-in-the-geometric-direction' quotient of the arithmetic-and-symmetric fundamental group of (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3). It is an extension of Γ by M̂.

Diagram (282) compares two extensions:
- the top row, 1 → M̂ → M̃ → Γ → 1;
- the bottom row, the group G_{ρ,σ̃} = Ẑ^* · M̃ from earlier sections, an extension of Ẑ^* × S_3 by M̂.
The vertical maps are the identity on M̂ and χ × id_{S_3} on the quotients, where χ is the cyclotomic character. This encodes the fact that Galois acts on the abelianized fundamental group only through χ.

Argument of the page:
1. The extension G_{ρ,σ̃} of Ẑ^* × S_3 by M̂ was found to be split. Since the top row is the pullback along χ × id, the extension M̃ of Γ by M̂ is split too.
2. Grothendieck notes this also follows from the existence of the Fermat tower (the curves x^n + y^n = 1, i.e. the abelian covers of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, defined over Q) together with the general 'réflexions' of the preceding pages on splittings and descent.
3. Moreover there is a unique M̂-conjugacy class of splittings of G_{ρ,σ̃}. Pulled back, it gives a canonical (but a priori not unique) M̂-conjugacy class of splittings of M̃ → Γ.
4. Such a class amounts to a canonical M̂-conjugacy class of liftings of the Γ-action to the maximal abelian cover X_0 of X = M_{0,3,Q̄}. Equivalently, it is a functor on Π(M_{0,3,Q}, S_3) with values in groups or profinite groups.
5. Next page: a canonical S_3-equivariant Q-model ('dessin') of the abelian tower, isomorphic to the covering found above.

Marginal note: 'H^1(Γ, M̂) est un groupe fort gros! — Mais non, cf. th. p. 716'. This is a self-correction: the obstruction to uniqueness, H^1(Γ_Q × S_3, M̂), turns out not to be large.
- By Hochschild–Serre, the S_3-part H^1(S_3, M̂^{Γ_Q}) vanishes, since Ẑ(1)^{Γ_Q} = 0.
- What remains is (Q^{*∧} ⊗ (Z^3/diag))^{S_3}, using Kummer theory for H^1(Γ_Q, Ẑ(1)).
- These invariants are at most small torsion, because (Z^3/diag)^{S_3} = 0 up to 3-torsion phenomena.

Purpose: this is a step in the 'Longue Marche' program. The goal is to describe Galois-equivariant, S_3-equivariant structures on the tower of covers of P^1 − 3 points, here at the abelian (Fermat) level, toward a description of the Galois action via 'dessins'.
errors: The deduction 'the bottom extension splits, hence the pulled-back extension splits' is correct: the pullback of a split extension is split.

'Canonical but non-unique' is slightly overstated, as Grothendieck's own margin admits. The ambiguity is measured by H^1(Γ_Q × S_3, M̂), which by Kummer theory plus S_3-invariants is at most a small torsion group, not 'fort gros'. The margin defers this to a theorem on p. 716.

The claim that the extension G_{ρ,σ̃} has a unique conjugacy class of splittings (vanishing of H^1(Ẑ^* × S_3, M̂)) is quoted from earlier pages and not verified here. At l = 2 and l = 3, small torsion contributions are possible and would need checking.

ideas.what: Galois action on the abelianized geometric fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞} factors through the cyclotomic character (diagram (282)).
ideas.modern_name: Π^ab ≅ Ẑ(1)^2; Galois action through χ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Kummer theory); Ihara, Anderson–Ihara, Deligne for the metabelian/pro-unipotent refinements (1986–89)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated); not as such in the Esquisse

ideas.what: Splitting of the extension of Γ_Q × S_3 by Π̂^ab, and its relation to the Fermat tower being defined over Q.
ideas.modern_name: Section of the metabelian/abelian fundamental group extension via rational (tangential) base points; Fermat curves as the abelian tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Fermat curves, 'Profinite braid groups...', Annals 1986); Anderson; Deligne 1989

ideas.what: Uniqueness up to conjugation of S_3-equivariant splittings, controlled by H^1(Γ_Q × S_3, M̂), and a canonical descent of the abelian tower with its S_3-symmetry to Q (as a functor on the fundamental groupoid of (M_{0,3,Q}, S_3)).
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant descent / section conjecture at the abelian level; S_3-symmetric tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Ihara, Schmidt–Stix); GT-theory (Drinfeld, Ihara)

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out an S_3-equivariant canonical descent of the abelian (Fermat) tower of P^1 − 3 points to Q, phrased as a functor on the fundamental groupoid of the stack-like pair (M_{0,3,Q}, S_3). He explicitly computes the size of the ambiguity, H^1(Γ_Q × S_3, M̂), with a theorem on p. 716. The content is known in substance (Ihara, Anderson, Deligne), but this particular groupoid/equivariant formulation and the H^1 computation are a modest unpublished detail.
missed.quote: Cela définit donc une classe de M̂-conjugaison canonique de relèvements sur 𝔛 = M_{0,3 Q̄} de l'action de Γ à 𝔛_0 — ou ce qui revient au même, un foncteur sur Π(M_{0,3 Q}, S_3)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: it fits the GT/anabelian treatment of symmetric base points but adds no evident new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard facts about the abelianized fundamental group of P^1 − 3 points and the Fermat tower, known from Ihara/Anderson/Deligne in the mid-1980s. The equivariant groupoid formulation is characteristic of Grothendieck but not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Top-right label: Γ = N_{0,3} = Γ_Q × S_3 (the previous page writes Π_Q × S_3); the vertical map is χ × id_{S_3}, χ the cyclotomic character.
The bottom group should be G_{ρ,σ̃} (rho, sigma-tilde), consistent with the previous page, not 'G_{p,σ}^∼'.
Left vertical arrow is an isomorphism ('≀'), i.e. the identity of M̂.

'comme les auteurs l'ont trouvé' is doubtful; more plausibly 'comme on l'a [vu/trouvé]' (something like 'les calculs'). The handwriting is unclear; 'auteurs' does not fit Grothendieck's own earlier computation.
Parenthesis: the struck-out 'ce qui paraît' is replaced by an insertion read as 'a dessein fait' (uncertain), followed by 'est aussi conséquence de l'existence de la tour de Fermat'.
'𝔛_0' appears to be the abelian (Fermat) cover of 𝔛; the insertion 'sur 𝔛 = M_{0,3 Q̄}' is correct.
Margin: 'NB H^1(Γ, M̂) est un groupe fort gros! — Mais non, cf. th. p. 716' is correct.
